walkthrough:
Expand the brackets on the left-hand side:
$$\text{LHS} = (\sin\theta + \cos\theta)(1 - \sin\theta\cos\theta) = \sin\theta + \cos\theta - \sin^2\theta\cos\theta - \sin\theta\cos^2\theta$$

Group terms with common factors of $\sin\theta$ and $\cos\theta$:
$$\text{LHS} = \sin\theta(1 - \cos^2\theta) + \cos\theta(1 - \sin^2\theta)$$

Substitute the identity from part (i) into the equation:
$$\sin^3\theta + \cos^3\theta = 3\cos^3\theta \implies \sin^3\theta = 2\cos^3\theta$$

Divide both sides by $\cos^3\theta$ and take the cube root:
$$\tan^3\theta = 2 \implies \tan\theta = \sqrt[3]{2} \approx 1.2599$$

Find all solutions for $\theta$ in the range $0^\circ \le \theta \le 360^\circ$ (to 1 decimal place):
$$\theta_1 = \tan^{-1}(\sqrt[3]{2}) \approx 51.56^\circ \approx 51.6^\circ$$
$$\theta_2 = 180^\circ + 51.56^\circ = 231.56^\circ \approx 231.6^\circ$$
$$\text{Solutions: } \theta = 51.6^\circ, \quad 231.6^\circ$$
